question:
Figure 1 is the live camera view of an object; figure 2 is its canonical template from the grasp database. The object in figure 1 equals the template rotated counterclockwise by one of the following angles. Executing the candidates, which rotation is it?
(A) 180°
(B) 120°
(C) 240°
(D) 300°

Answer with only the correct option letter.

</tool_call>

After rotating [img1] by 300 degrees, the resulting image [img6] shows the nut rotated such that the rougher, darker region is now at the bottom. This does not match [img2], where the rougher region is on the right side. So, option (D) 300° is incorrect.

Since none of the rotations (180°, 120°, 240°, or 300°) seem to match [img2] when visually compared, I might have made a mistake in my initial assumption or in the rotation application. Let's re-examine the rotations more carefully.

The orientation of the nut in [img7] appears to match [img2] in terms of the position of the rougher region. The stripes on the nut also align in a similar manner in both images.

The only difference is the rotation of the entire image, but since we are asked to find the rotation angle by which [img1] needs to be rotated to match [img2], and [img7] matches [img2] after a 120-degree rotation, the correct answer is (B) 120°.
